subject: Interregion traffic realignment and tenant failover checklist
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir.patel@acme-retail.com>, Tina Wu <tina.wu@globex.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: [ACTION] Immediate traffic realignment for impacted regions — brief and next steps

Hi Samir / Tina —

We detected elevated failures and tail latency for a subset of instances serving EU and APAC customers starting ~07:40 UTC. Our automated routing layer initiated temporary rerouting to healthy capacity in US regions for affected tenants while our infra team investigates.

We wanted to provide a short-facing note and the immediate customer actions you should expect:
- What happened: network peering flaps plus a throttling condition on a storage tier in the EU datacenter leading to increased request errors for long-running streams.
- Immediate action taken: prefix-level reroute to US serving region for impacted tenants (transparent to most requests).
- What you might see: increased latency for previously EU-hosted tenants and transient 5xxs for in-flight sessions during the switch window (typically <2m).
- Your expected impact: most requests will continue to succeed; we saw a 6–12% increase in p50/p95 latency for a short window during the change.

Attachments: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf (customer-facing steps), tenant-failover-mapping.csv (mapping of tenant -> preferred fallback).

Next steps we own:
1) Confirm per-tenant mapping and keep reroute active until EU/APAC peering stabilizes.
2) Provide a bridge and live updates (see link below).
3) After stabilization, we will coordinate controlled backfill to original regions.

Bridge: https://zoom.us/j/000000000 (ops bridge)
Status page: https://status.redwoodinfra.internal/incidents/2029-07-14-traffic-shift

We expect to stabilize within the hour; I’ll follow up with a one-paragraph customer-facing summary for your teams.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Support, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_runbook_v2.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]

Thanks Ben — appreciate the quick heads up. A couple of quick questions for our SREs:
1) Will our public endpoints or IP prefixes change as part of the temporary reroute? We need to know for our firewall rules.
2) Any tenant-level opt-outs? A small set of workloads (payment gateway) must remain pinned to EU despite higher latency.

If you can confirm those two points we can escalate to our infra team if needed. We’re on standby for the bridge.

—Samir

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 08:34:12 -0700
Subject: Re: [ACTION] Immediate traffic realignment for impacted regions — brief and next steps

Samir — quick answers from infra ops:

1) IP prefixes: No public endpoint changes. The reroute is at the application-load balancing layer and preserves the same public hostnames and TLS certificates. You will not need to update firewall allow-lists unless you have IP whitelists that check origin ASN ranges — in that case, allowlist the US egress ranges listed in tenant-failover-mapping.csv.

2) Tenant-level opt-outs: yes — customers can opt their tenant to remain pinned to the original region. For any tenant that must remain in EU, we will apply a policy tag that prevents automatic reroute; this will preserve locality but may expose the tenant to degraded availability until the EU peering is stable. To request that, reply to this message with the tenant IDs (or use the mapping CSV).

Operational notes (what we’re doing now):
- Rolling traffic to US capacity and watching for dropped streams.
- Applying read-only mode on a small set of internal control planes while we validate storage tier health.
- Debugging storage throttling with the vendor (cloudcorp); vendor-ops has been engaged.

Estimated timeline: initial mitigation active now; targeted verification in 30–45 minutes; full backfill after peering stability confirmed (~1–3 hours).

[Attachment: tenant-failover-mapping.csv (CSV, 12KB)]

—
Laura Bennett
Operations Engineer, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 09:02:55 -0700
Subject: Customer-facing update: brief status, impact, and actions required (please share)

Hi Samir / Tina —

Short update for your teams that you can redistribute to product and platform stakeholders:

Summary: Starting 07:40 UTC an EU peering degradation and a storage throttling condition caused increased errors and latency for a subset of customers in EU and APAC. We initiated a transparent reroute to US capacity for affected tenants; the majority of traffic continued to succeed with a small latency increase.

What we did:
• Automatically rerouted affected prefixes to US serving capacity. No hostname or TLS changes.
• Engaged cloud vendor for storage tier throttling and pulled read-only config for a small control plane to reduce load.
• Notified impacted customers and opened ops bridge.

What you will need to do:
• If you have strict IP allow-lists, allow the US egress ranges in the attached CSV.
• To keep a tenant pinned in its original region, reply with tenant IDs (we will apply an opt-out policy).

Timings:
• Mitigation in place: 07:50 UTC
• Verification expected: ongoing over the next 45 minutes
• Estimated full normalization: 1–3 hours (contingent on vendor stability)

We will send a follow-up once we begin controlled backfill to EU/APAC and after the vendor confirms the underlying storage issue is resolved. Please escalate any business-critical workloads to me directly.

Bridge & logs: https://zoom.us/j/000000000 | https://logs.redwoodinfra.internal/incident/2029-07-14
Status: https://status.redwoodinfra.internal/incidents/2029-07-14-traffic-shift

Thanks for your patience — we’ll keep updates frequent.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Support, Redwood Inference

Date: Sun, 14 Jul 2029 14:52:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident note and next steps — action: validate and close

Hi Tina / Samir —

Final update: the vendor confirmed storage throttling root cause (misconfigured quota enforcement during a maintenance window) at ~11:10 UTC. We ran a controlled backfill from US -> EU/APAC beginning 12:05 UTC and completed the migration back at 13:24 UTC. Post-backfill checks show error rates returned to baseline and tail latency normalized.

Items for customers:
• Tenant opt-outs: we applied the opt-out for tenant-aurora-payments as requested.
• Session tokens: we confirmed session tokens were preserved for successful requests; a small subset of in-flight requests during the switch experienced auth errors — per-tenant retry is the recommended mitigation.
• Action required: please validate that your critical flows are operating normally and reply with any residual anomalies.

Planned postmortem: we will publish a technical postmortem and a vendor timeline on Mon 2029-07-15 by 10:00 UTC. The postmortem will include remediation actions (improved quota alerting, tighter pre-maintenance gating for vendor actions, and a longer stabilization window before automated backfills).

If you want a walk-through of the postmortem, we can schedule a short readout with our engineering leads (Marcus and Grace).

Thanks again for your patience and the quick coordination — please confirm when you’ve validated your traffic flows.

—
Ben Carter
Head of Support, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
